# Altair sample disks that this gateway is known to run.
#
# Generated by `record_altairduino_manifest` -- do not edit by hand.  Each line
# is NAME<TAB>BYTES<TAB>SHA256<TAB>SOURCE<TAB>NOTE.  The hash is of the bytes the
# pinned URL really served, checked against the local copy this project booted,
# and those same served bytes were then cold-started -- so every disk here is
# one that boots, not one that was believed to.
#
# SOURCE names a repository and folder in `SOURCES` (src/cpm/fetch.rs):
#   hansel       github.com/dhansel/Altair8800  (disks/)
#                pinned at 3a42f6646c193567f1c9859c3fa1d06126088490
#   duino        github.com/jpmcneely/AltairDuino-Disks  (original/)
#                pinned at 95a2324461f39562be9f46762b7b22cf1afec445
#   duino-extra  github.com/jpmcneely/AltairDuino-Disks  (extra/)
#                pinned at 95a2324461f39562be9f46762b7b22cf1afec445
#
# Two repositories because neither contains the other.  Hansel's DISK13-DISK16
# are CP/M 3.0 disk 1 and 2, Felix and CP/M 2.2 MITS+Tarbell, and are documented
# as such; McNeely's four files of those names are DIFFERENT disks, undocumented
# in its own catalogue, one of which does not boot.  So the contested names come
# from Hansel and only the five McNeely uniquely has come from McNeely.
#
# The disks are not ours and are not shipped -- this fetches them from the
# original repositories on the operator's behalf.  The vintage software on them
# belongs to MITS, Microsoft, Digital Research and Infocom.
#
# Offered by neither screen because they did not cold-start when this
# was generated -- data companions that carry no boot program:
#   DISK0B.DSK (this image has no boot sector - it is data, not a system disk)
#   DISK0D.DSK (this image has no boot sector - it is data, not a system disk)
#   DISK0F.DSK (this image has no boot sector - it is data, not a system disk)
#   TDISK06.DSK (this image has no boot sector - it is data, not a system disk)
#
